name: Egalitarianism
summary: Egalitarianism holds that all people are equal in fundamental worth and should be treated as equals, in law, politics and, for most strands, in the distribution of resources and social standing. Strands differ over what to equalize (resources, welfare, capabilities) and whether the aim is distribution or relations of equal standing; most support redistribution through taxation and public services while accepting markets and individual liberties.
scope: The mainstream of contemporary egalitarian political philosophy as presented in the Stanford Encyclopedia entry (Rawls, Dworkin, Sen, Anderson and luck and relational egalitarians) and the equal-rights tradition of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights. It treats egalitarianism as a family close to social democracy and liberal egalitarianism. Marxist, anarchist and Christian egalitarian strands are noted but not taken as the core, so many answers on revolution, public ownership and class are split or low confidence.

furtherReading.note: Clear survey of the main egalitarian positions and policies.

furtherReading.title: John Rawls (Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy)
furtherReading.note: Introduces the most influential egalitarian theory of justice.

furtherReading.title: Universal Declaration of Human Rights
furtherReading.note: The best-known statement of equal rights and dignity.

keyFigures.name: John Rawls
keyFigures.role: Developed justice as fairness, including the difference principle and fair equality of opportunity.

keyFigures.name: Ronald Dworkin
keyFigures.role: Developed resource egalitarianism and the luck egalitarian distinction between brute and option luck.

keyFigures.name: Elizabeth Anderson
keyFigures.role: Pioneered relational egalitarianism, which treats equality as a relation among members of a community.

sources.title: John Rawls
sources.author: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy
sources.usedFor: Property-owning democracy, difference principle, healthcare, fair value of political liberties.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Rawls holds the state must guarantee basic health care, and universal healthcare appears in the egalitarian policy toolkit.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Inferred: a job guarantee and reduced inequality of income are standard egalitarian aims, though the wage mechanism is not specified.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Egalitarians accept markets for efficiency (Rawls, Dworkin) but deny that unregulated markets allocate justly, so they reject the claim as stated.

public-ownership.rationale: Adherents split: socialist egalitarians favor social ownership while Rawlsians prefer property-owning democracy and regulated markets.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Wealth taxes and progressive taxation are named egalitarian policies for curbing inequality.

unions-good.rationale: Inferred from egalitarian interest in democratizing workplace power and relational equality of standing.

property-fundamental.rationale: Egalitarians treat property as subordinate to fair distribution; Rawls lists personal property but not unrestricted productive property among basic liberties.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Inferred from concern that concentrated private economic power undermines political equality and equal standing.

cut-welfare.rationale: Social security and income support are central egalitarian tools; cutting them contradicts the doctrine.

worker-ownership.rationale: Worker-managed firms appear in Rawls's liberal socialism but adherents split on whether they are required.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Inferred: priority of basic liberties in Rawls's account weighs against surveillance trade-offs.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Egalitarianism is largely silent on drug policy; adherents split.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Adherents split between protecting equal dignity (UDHR) and the priority of basic liberties such as speech.

strong-leader.rationale: Egalitarian management aims to spread power and decision-making; a leader bypassing gridlock concentrates it.

state-harmful.rationale: Egalitarian policy relies on state institutions to secure equality, so the state is not seen as unnecessary.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed by egalitarian theory; adherents split.

empower-police-military.rationale: Inferred: no egalitarian case for expanded coercive powers, and concern for equal protection and non-discrimination.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Egalitarian feminists split between choice and exploitation views.

decide-locally.rationale: Egalitarianism is neutral on level of government, though equal treatment favors uniform national standards.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred from equal dignity and concern for the disadvantaged.

traditional-family.rationale: Egalitarians (Okin) criticize traditional gendered family roles as unequal.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Equal rights without distinction of any kind is the core legal-egalitarian principle.

abortion-legal.rationale: Inferred from gender-equality arguments of egalitarian feminists.

more-religion-public.rationale: Rawls's public reason model keeps comprehensive doctrines out of political justification.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Reparations and anti-discrimination measures are in the egalitarian toolkit, and civil-rights egalitarianism opposed segregation.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Gender egalitarianism concerns equal treatment and is not tied to a view of gender's origin.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Egalitarianism is universalist; preservation of tradition is not a concern, though not opposed either.

gradual-change.rationale: Egalitarians are split between reformist (Rawls) and revolutionary (Marxist) strands.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Inferred from universal equal worth; some egalitarians nevertheless defend border limits.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The UDHR frames equal rights internationally; global egalitarians favor stronger institutions.

free-trade.rationale: Not addressed; egalitarians split by effects on the worse off.

nation-first.rationale: Equal moral worth of all humans in the UDHR weighs against national priority.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Inferred from the human-rights tradition that grounds egalitarianism.

open-borders.rationale: Global egalitarians favor it; others defend limits. Genuinely split.

limit-growth.rationale: Egalitarianism is indifferent to growth as such.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Inferred: climate harms fall on the worse off, which egalitarians prioritize.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Egalitarianism holds that unjust distribution, not technology, is the problem.

revolution-justified.rationale: Marxist egalitarians say yes while Rawlsian liberal egalitarians prefer reform; split.

experts-over-public.rationale: Democratic equality and equal standing weigh against rule by experts.

central-planning.rationale: Rawls rejects a command economy as concentrating too much state power and threatening political equality.

socialized-markets.rationale: Rawls's liberal socialism with worker-managed firms or property-owning democracy accept markets under such ownership.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not a defining egalitarian measure; adherents split.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inheritance is a named area of egalitarian economic regulation and wealth-tax proposals curb accumulation.

basic-income.rationale: Universal basic income is in the egalitarian policy toolkit, though debated.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Rawls prefers decentralised markets; other egalitarians accept industrial policy.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Property-owning democracy spreads productive assets widely, which Rawls prefers to welfare capitalism.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Mainstream egalitarianism keeps markets and wages; only Marxist strands seek abolition.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Inferred: no egalitarian rationale and conflicts with state economic stewardship.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Inferred: egalitarianism does not endorse state-recognized corporate bodies.

one-party-rule.rationale: Equal suffrage and the fair value of political liberties require pluralist democracy.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Hereditary rank contradicts equal worth and political equality.

democracy-best.rationale: Equal suffrage and the equal value of political liberties are central egalitarian commitments.

direct-votes.rationale: Egalitarians favor democratizing power but are split on direct versus representative forms.

workers-councils.rationale: Marxist and libertarian-socialist strands say yes; liberal egalitarians say no.

natural-rulers.rationale: Egalitarianism is defined in opposition to elitism and holds all persons equal in worth.

political-violence-never.rationale: Pacifist and reformist strands agree, Marxist strands do not.

war-builds-character.rationale: Inferred: foreign to egalitarian concern with equal dignity and welfare.

separate-church-state.rationale: Equal freedom of religion for all and Rawls's public reason favor separation.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Public justification to citizens of all doctrines is not met by scriptural law, though Christian egalitarians cite scripture for equality.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Rawls requires equal protection through public institutions.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Equality without distinction of race and opposition to segregation is core.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Marxist strands affirm it; liberal egalitarians do not.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Sources say egalitarianism generally advocates equality of opportunity, while substantive and outcome-based strands go further; adherents are split.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Reparations are in the egalitarian toolkit, though applied here by inference.

civilizational-union.rationale: Inferred from universalism over civilizational grouping.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Egalitarians stress reciprocity and equal concern, not self-interest as a virtue.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Rights equal for all, with priority of basic liberties, outweigh communal duties.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Some egalitarians extend equality to animals; most are silent.

limit-population.rationale: Egalitarian sources never address population policy, so adherents have no settled view.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Inferred: egalitarians seek fairer distribution within modern society, not rejection of it.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Inferred; foraging societies are cited as egalitarian by anthropologists but no political program follows.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Egalitarian sources never address the pace of technological change, so adherents have no settled view.

human-enhancement.rationale: Luck egalitarians worry about unequal access to enhancement; split.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Inferred from democratic accountability and equal standing.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Egalitarian sources do not address encryption, so adherents have no settled view on it.

restore-past-order.rationale: Egalitarianism challenges inherited hierarchy and is progressive in orientation.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Egalitarian sources do not address this, and adherents hold principled commitments yet value outcomes.

means-match-ends.rationale: Anarchist egalitarians say yes; others are indifferent.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Mainstream egalitarianism accepts specialization with fair terms.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Rawls and luck egalitarians reward effort and permit incentive inequalities, though Marxist need is cited as an egalitarian ideal.

production-for-use.rationale: Marxist egalitarians affirm it; liberal egalitarians accept markets.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Marx's exploitation critique supports redistribution, but liberal egalitarians do not adopt it.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Rawls and most egalitarians reject concentrated class-based state power.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Marxist strands affirm; others do not.

taxation-theft.rationale: Rothbard's critique of egalitarianism treats taxation as theft; egalitarians reject this.

harm-principle.rationale: Liberal egalitarians accept it, while others favor further state action; split.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Egalitarian theories center individuals, but group-based equality and social equity are also advanced.

conscription.rationale: Rawls allows conscription only for national defense; adherents split.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Equal suffrage and fair value of political liberties are prioritized.

state-as-business.rationale: Citizens hold equal rights and standing, not customer status.

positive-liberty.rationale: Sen's effective freedoms and Rawls's worth of liberty tie freedom to material means.

media-academia-power.rationale: Egalitarians stress private economic power over politics, not media and academia.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Equal worth without distinction of race; egalitarians oppose such claims.

organic-representation.rationale: Equal and universal suffrage is the egalitarian norm.

total-state.rationale: Rawls prioritizes basic liberties against state direction of all life.

bound-labor.rationale: Equal rights and freedom, and the UDHR bars slavery or servitude.

universal-morality.rationale: Equal moral worth is posited universally, as in the UDHR and Rawls.

single-common-good.rationale: Rawls emphasizes reasonable pluralism and fair terms among diverse interests.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Egalitarian sources never address diaspora return rights, so adherents have no settled view.

revive-national-language.rationale: Egalitarian sources never address language revival, so adherents have no settled view.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Egalitarian management aims to democratize decision-making and relational egalitarians scrutinize workplace hierarchy.

school-vouchers.rationale: Rawls favors fair equality of opportunity in education through public provision.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Inferred: egalitarian programs often rely on public spending.

economic-freedom.rationale: Rawls says political equality requires limiting economic power, not liberating it.

rule-by-example.rationale: The rule of law and equal protection are egalitarian foundations.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Rawls allows reasonable religious doctrines; adherents split.

national-self-determination.rationale: Egalitarian sources never address national self-determination, so adherents are split.

force-without-un.rationale: Inferred from the international human-rights order.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Social security as a right of everyone as a member of society and without discrimination.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Basic income and benefits without stigma or bureaucratic discretion are favored.

class-collaboration.rationale: Liberal egalitarians accept cooperation while Marxist strands say conflict.

dominated-front.rationale: Egalitarian sources never address anti-Western fronts, so adherents are split.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Gender egalitarianism and equal rights without distinction of sex.

ban-interest.rationale: Rawls accepts markets and credit; not addressed by egalitarianism.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Martin Luther King Jr. opposed segregation on egalitarian grounds and the UDHR bars discrimination by race.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Marxist strands affirm; liberal egalitarians do not.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Inferred from concern for climate harms to the worse off.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Equal rights without distinction implies no demand to give up culture.

elite-replacement.rationale: Conspiracy claim rejected; egalitarians oppose its racial premises.

proportional-representation.rationale: Equal suffrage is often held to favor equal weight of votes.

national-mission.rationale: Inferred: egalitarianism is universalist and not missionary.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Gender egalitarians and Young's account of oppression treat structural disadvantage as real.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Equal worth and basic liberties oppose coercive eugenics.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Equal protection of the law and accountability for abuses are implied by legal egalitarianism.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Egalitarian policies require a state much larger than a minimal state; Rawls rejects laissez-faire.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Equal worth without distinction of race.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Equal fundamental worth and equality before the law are the defining egalitarian claims, stated in the UDHR.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Not an egalitarian question; the Rawlsian mainstream is silent and only the Marxist strand holds it, so adherents are split.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Egalitarians condemn displacement as unjust but split on whether settler states count as colonial; inferred from equal-rights principles.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Equal treatment before the law without distinction of religion fits the equal-rights tradition, though some egalitarians accept group accommodations.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Freedom to change religion is protected in the Universal Declaration (Art. 18), so legal limits on conversion are rejected.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Inferred: banning a practice to honor one religion's beliefs conflicts with equal standing for all citizens.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Inferred from equal standing for citizens of all faiths (relational egalitarianism); not a stated egalitarian position.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Inferred: mainstream egalitarians favor accountable, limited security powers and do not hold a socialist-state theory.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The Declaration says the will of the people is the basis of government authority, and Rawlsian justice rests on terms free equals could accept.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Mainstream egalitarian philosophy assumes facts can be known fairly while criticizing unequal distribution; inferred.

trade-surplus.rationale: Trade balances are not an egalitarian aim; what matters is the distribution of resources and capabilities; inferred.

population-transfer.rationale: The UDHR bars arbitrary exile and discrimination and protects the right to leave and return.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Egalitarians accept taxation and public provision as justified coercion, so initiating force is not always wrong.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Egalitarians emphasise cooperation and shared institutions over competition as the route to justice; inferred.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Rawls allows limits on the intolerant when liberty itself is at stake; inferred from the liberal egalitarian tradition.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Relational egalitarians define equality as freedom from domination and hierarchy of standing.

separated-powers.rationale: Liberal egalitarians support constitutional democracy with checks on power; inferred.

vanguard-party.rationale: Mainstream egalitarianism is democratic and not committed to a leading revolutionary party; inferred.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The difference principle and priority views give weight to the worst off.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Inferred: egalitarians favour broad ownership but split on whether selling public housing serves equality.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: The Declaration protects the right to form and join trade unions, which egalitarians treat as a way to equalise bargaining power.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Egalitarians hold that unjust institutions, not numbers, explain lasting poverty.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Equal dignity and non-discrimination apply regardless of race or origin, so diversity is not a ground for treating people unequally.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Lottery is a recognised equalising device but egalitarians are split on replacing elections.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Equal protection and fair trial rights are central and the Declaration limits their suspension.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Egalitarians accept price controls for basic needs but the question is not a defining issue; inferred.

party-controls-media.rationale: The Declaration protects freedom of opinion and of seeking and sharing information.

party-commands-army.rationale: Inferred from the Declaration's principle that government rests on the will of the people through genuine elections.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Inferred from equal-treatment principles and the right to a nationality, which favour easy access to citizenship.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Inferred: equal standing in politics is central, but egalitarian philosophy does not set public-office pay, and many accept competitive pay.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Inferred: liberal egalitarians stress each citizen's equal political voice and independent judgment, not binding party discipline.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Inferred: cosmopolitan egalitarians accept shared institutions for global justice, though the field is split on this.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Inferred: equal political liberty and fair value of political rights point toward legislative and accountable control over executive power.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Inferred: the equal-standing ideal and freedom of religion in the UDHR favour no privileged hierarchy, though church governance is not addressed.

clerical-rule.rationale: Equal rights regardless of religion and equal political liberty exclude clergy holding final authority.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Inferred: the liberal egalitarian mainstream accepts national defence and does not endorse working for one's own government's defeat.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Rawlsian egalitarians protect freedom of expression as a basic liberty and reject state perfectionism.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Inferred: equal political rights do not settle term limits, and adherents can go either way.

recall-officials.rationale: Inferred: equal and effective political participation is valued, but recall is not part of the mainstream egalitarian program.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Foreign policy is outside egalitarian theory; adherents split on alliances, inferred from the family's scope.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Egalitarians favour access to housing but rarely a ban on renting; inferred from the focus on fair distribution rather than ownership.

people-in-arms.rationale: Not addressed by egalitarian theory; inferred mainstream preference for professional forces under democratic control.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Egalitarians have no case for the moral superiority of rural over urban people, inferred from equal-worth principles.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: National reunification is not an egalitarian issue; adherents split, inferred.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Egalitarians stress equal standing for all, so judging the educated as out of touch is not a position they hold; inferred.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Equal worth of persons is not the same as equal cultures, but relational egalitarians reject ranking people's ways of life; inferred.

death-penalty.rationale: The UDHR protects the right to life and bars cruel punishment, which most egalitarians read as ruling out execution.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: The UDHR calls for equal rights of men and women and a right to education, supporting teaching gender equality.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Egalitarians favour shared public education grounded in science; inferred, not a stated egalitarian position.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Adherents split: some relational egalitarians and feminists favour limits, others stress equal liberty, inferred.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Equal standing for all residents and the UDHR right to a nationality count against descent-only citizenship; inferred.

minority-language-support.rationale: Equal standing for minorities supports public language support, inferred from relational egalitarianism.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Rawls-style equal liberty favours conscience, but luck egalitarians doubt exemptions; adherents split, inferred.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Rawlsian liberty and Mill-style experiments in living support plural ways of life, inferred.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Not a core egalitarian topic; inferred from global-egalitarian concern for the worst off that cancelling unpayable poor-country debt is favoured.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred: egalitarians care about who holds economic power, so formal independence alone is seen as insufficient, though the family is not unified on this.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Inferred from the commitment to equal political voice and suffrage; an elected assembly fits, though mainstream egalitarians do not insist on it.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The UDHR and Rawls give priority to equal basic political liberties, which are not to be traded for economic gains.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Cosmopolitan and global egalitarians hold that nationality does not weaken duties to the poor, though some egalitarians limit justice to compatriots.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Egalitarianism does not address nuclear deterrence; no clear inference from its principles.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Inferred from equal suffrage in the UDHR; direct election is the more egalitarian method, but the issue is not central.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Egalitarians split between insulating monetary policy from politics and keeping it democratically accountable; not a defining issue.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Inferred: egalitarian universalism gives little weight to historic territorial claims, and peace is typically valued above them.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Rawls's property-owning democracy and the egalitarian toolkit treat ownership as shaped by what justice requires of the whole community.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Egalitarians do not take a position on the USSR's class character; this is a debate internal to Marxism.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Inferred: equal protection of everyone, especially the vulnerable, supports precaution, though egalitarian texts do not address it.

collective-defense.rationale: Inferred from Rawls's account of just peoples defending themselves; alliances are not an egalitarian topic as such.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Inferred from equal respect for persons and peoples; consent is the egalitarian test of legitimate rule.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Equal liberty of conscience and freedom of religion are protected equal rights, so egalitarians resist state control of churches.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Egalitarianism does not address the form of head of state; adherents split between republics and ceremonial monarchies.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Inferred: the equal standing of citizens implies consent matters, so force against an unwilling region is hard to justify.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Inferred: nothing in egalitarianism requires one uniform system, provided the region's residents keep equal rights.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Equal dignity and rights are incompatible with a hereditary ruler of divine rank.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Progressive taxation is a standard egalitarian instrument and the difference principle justifies redistribution that a flat rate would not deliver.

character-from-environment.rationale: Luck egalitarianism treats unchosen circumstances and upbringing as the main source of unequal outcomes, which is why it seeks to equalize them.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Equality before the law means rulers are bound by the same laws as everyone else.

space-expansion.rationale: Inferred: egalitarian priority goes to distributive and social justice on Earth, and space goals are not part of the tradition.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Inferred: equal political standing and fair value of political liberties favour equal democratic participation over reserved aristocratic power.

leader-cult.rationale: Equal standing of citizens is at odds with glorifying a leader as the embodiment of the nation.

equal-parenting.rationale: Inferred from equal rights of spouses at and after dissolution of marriage and gender equality; a rebuttable equal-time presumption fits, though not a specific egalitarian doctrine.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Inferred: mainstream liberal egalitarians reject class struggle as a theory and accept markets.

land-redistribution.rationale: Inferred: Rawls's property-owning democracy aims at wide ownership of assets, which could include land.

refugee-return.rationale: Inferred from the UDHR right to return to one's country; the extension to descendants is not stated.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Inferred: equal dignity regardless of nationality weighs against claims based on ethnicity.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The UDHR protects the freedom to change one's religion.

women-must-cover.rationale: Equal rights and freedom of belief are central to the UDHR, so compelled dress for women is rejected.

common-currency.rationale: Not addressed; egalitarians split on a shared currency.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Inferred: universal equal worth goes against unions based on shared ancestry.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Inferred from the UDHR's protection of cultural life and education.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Inferred from the UDHR's equal rights for all wherever they live.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Inferred: egalitarians mostly hold that moral argument drives reform, though Marxist strands disagree.

ban-cartels.rationale: Inferred: concentrated economic power undermines fair value of political liberties.

no-bailouts.rationale: Inferred: egalitarians dislike rewarding failure but also support rescuing jobs; adherents split.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Rawls holds basic liberties and equal rights should be entrenched against majority decision.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Inferred from the UDHR's equal access to public service.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Inferred: egalitarians favour global justice and open exchange over self-sufficiency.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Inferred from UDHR labour rights, which could be written into agreements.

moral-incentives.rationale: Inferred: Rawls and luck egalitarians accept material incentives if they help the worst off.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Inferred: egalitarians favour democratic means; the UDHR treats rebellion as a last resort.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Equal standing regardless of birth is central, and the UDHR bars distinctions based on birth.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Inferred from equal worth of all peoples; egalitarians favour history that treats all peoples fairly, though many accept a national core.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Equal moral worth of all people rules out rule over others on a claim of advancement.

patriotic-education.rationale: Inferred from the universalist stance; the Declaration urges education for understanding among nations, not national pride.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Relational and luck egalitarians support race-conscious measures to remedy disadvantage, though some prefer class-based measures.

public-money-creation.rationale: Not addressed by egalitarian theory; egalitarians split on state-issued versus bank-created money.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Egalitarian liberalism assumes a regulated market economy that survives with redistribution, as in Rawls's property-owning democracy.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Inferred from equal standing among peoples; egalitarians generally reject special influence over former colonies.

delink-world-market.rationale: Egalitarians support global justice through fairer trade and aid rather than withdrawal from the world economy.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Egalitarianism holds that workers share a common claim to equal standing, and does not use the labour-aristocracy thesis.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Equal dignity and non-discrimination in the Declaration and equal-standing theories oppose private discrimination.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Egalitarians back entrenched equal rights, as in the Declaration and Rawls's priority of basic liberties, though some doubt judicial review.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Inferred from the equal right of peoples to self-determination in the egalitarian human-rights tradition.

elective-rulers.rationale: Equal political standing implies government by the will of the people expressed in elections, not hereditary rule.

minority-veto.rationale: Equal standing points to majority decision among equals; inferred, since Rawlsians also accept constitutional limits.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The Universal Declaration's preamble accepts rebellion against tyranny as a last resort when rights are not protected by law.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Inferred: egalitarians favor democratic legislatures over monarchs, though liberal egalitarians also accept constitutional review.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Inferred from the extension of equal moral concern by egalitarian thinkers; Rawls himself set animals aside.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Egalitarian thought is largely silent on this and adherents split.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Egalitarians ground help for the worse-off in justice owed as equals, not in the charity of the privileged; inferred.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Rawls stresses the fair value of political liberties and equal participation, which treats withdrawal as a loss.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Not a defining issue; the Marxist strand agrees, liberal egalitarians do not.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Hegemony theory belongs to the Marxist strand, which is not the core of this profile.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Rawls frames global duties as assistance, not exploitation; the Marxist strand differs, so adherents split.

native-born-offices.rationale: The Declaration gives every citizen equal access to public service and bars discrimination by origin.

party-own-road.rationale: Not an egalitarian issue; adherents have no common view.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Global egalitarians favor aid and redistribution between countries; inferred.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Inferred from the preference for equal rights of persons over national grievance.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Equal political standing for all citizens speaks against rule by descent group; inferred.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: The Declaration arose after fascism and rests on equal dignity; inferred that adherents would endorse the value.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Adherents split between condemning both and distinguishing them.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Egalitarians treat slavery as the gravest denial of equality and reject minimizing it; inferred, history not addressed.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Adherents split between preserving history and removing honors to oppressors.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Equal concern for disadvantage regardless of sex fits egalitarian principle; inferred.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Equal protection of the law under the Declaration implies equal services; inferred.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: The Declaration treats rights as universal and claims democratic government as a right of all peoples.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Egalitarians require civilian, democratic control of the state, not a political guardian role for the army.

paid-care-work.rationale: Inferred from relational egalitarians' concern with gendered inequality in unpaid work.

missingStatements.text: All people are of equal moral worth and should have equal rights before the law.
missingStatements.rationale: Equal fundamental worth and equality before the law are the defining egalitarian claims.

notes: Strands differ: Marxist and anarchist egalitarians would answer public ownership, class, revolution and need-based distribution more strongly; libertarian critics such as Rothbard reject the doctrine.
